summary: An excerpt from a fiction novel (Book 10, part 101) describing a CogRad wireless deployment in the Akwesasne woods, where the Rez will soon be unwired at 500 megabits per second. Elaine's crew and their Warrior escorts work together, and Lee-Daniel wins over the locals by example, leading to friendships with a teenaged Warrior called Mermaid and a middle-aged man called Cobra. Elaine gives Mermaid a surveying theodolite and booklet, and Lee-Daniel later sees her leading younger girls on surveying missions. The passage ends with a brief exchange where Lee-Daniel asks for privacy from the Series B man and MacDiarmid.
one_line: In a fiction excerpt, CogRad's wireless crews win over Akwesasne Warriors, including the girl Mermaid, while building a 500 Mbps network.
key_facts: CogRad's wireless gear pushed the project from a theoretical idea to a real success in Akwesahsne woods.
Within a week, the entire Rez would be unwired at 500 megabits/second.
Elaine's halts were treated as a nuisance by the frontmost Warrior, a girl of about 16, until she grew curious after the fifth halt.
Elaine handed the girl a can of pink spraychalk and directed her to mark the sight-lines.
The rear Warrior, a man of indeterminate age who wore a camou balaclava, rolled his eyes at the task.
Lee-Daniel gestured at a travois carrying the satellite tester, and the other Warrior took one end to help the juniors.
The girl introduced herself as "Mermaid" and the man introduced himself as "Cobra" by the time they reached the next ridge.
Cobra had a middle-aged face, handsome but for deep acne scars.
CogRad crews had never had explicit training in making friends with locals but learned from Lee-Daniel and middle-managers.
Elaine gave Mermaid a cheap theodolite with an integrated compass, GPS and altimeter, plus a little booklet on its use.
Lee-Daniel later saw Mermaid leading a group of even younger girls on surveying missions around the Indian School.
At a meeting, Lee-Daniel asked for privacy, and the Series B man said they were standing all the way over across the little table.
MacDiarmid led the Series B man and others back out to the communal area, after which Lee-Daniel flipped open his notebook.
